fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Forty Years From Guy's Hospital to the Sweat Lodge", "body": "Mortiboys traces a path from mainstream training at Guy's Hospital in London in the early 1980s, where he says he was already an outlier for hanging around the Stonehenge free festivals and playing Hawkwind, through travels in Australia and the Far East that included living with Aboriginal communities and the Mentawai tribe on Siberut off Sumatra. Back in the UK he moved through hypnotherapy, regression, neuro linguistics and a Tony Robbins course, kept a gong in his clinic for 32 years, sold his practice five years ago, and got word on the day of taping that a 12 acre Isle of Wight property was his."}, {"title": "Fear, White Coats and Courting a Dentist", "body": "Roughly 95 percent of dentistry, Mortiboys says, happens while the patient is wide awake and asked to surrender to a stranger, which is why he cites a UK figure of over 50 percent of people simply not going, with cost as the smoke screen. His advice on the relationship, not the treatment, is blunt: never jump into bed with a dentist, get an examination and a follow up first, and trust your intuition about their hands and intentions. He also blames the room itself, naming white coatitis, arguing sterile white reads as anti life, and describing his own turquoise walls, aromatherapy and patient painted ceiling art."}, {"title": "Teeth as Boundaries, Virility and the Inner Smile", "body": "Prompted by a neighbour's Alsatian barking through the recording, Mortiboys builds his symbolic reading of teeth: an animal shows canines to mark a boundary, so teeth stand for self empowerment and virility, and hiding them signals shame. He points to travellers he has met with brown or missing teeth whose inner smile, as he puts it, is so strong the outer one follows, and to betel nut chewers in India with bright red teeth. He is wary of cosmetic work, calling enamel removal for veneers enamel amputation, and notes agents telling singers aged 16 to 20 to get their teeth fixed fast."}, {"title": "Saliva as Oral Gold and the Vagus Nerve", "body": "The centre of Mortiboys' framework is saliva, which he calls oral gold and describes as a protective elixir that dries up in fight or flight and turns acidic under anxiety, poor breathing and reflux. He describes the waking pH check with litmus paper as the clue clinicians look at, and frames tooth decay as demineralisation, an osteoporosis of the teeth, since enamel is a crystal that dissolves in acid. Decay and gum disease are bifactorial in his view, an outside job and an inside job, and he links the shamanic staples of chanting, humming and drumming to published vagus nerve research."}, {"title": "Parasites, Hulda Clark and a Patient's Last Wish", "body": "Mortiboys contends that some gum cases which never respond to hygienist care are parasitic rather than bacterial, citing amoebic organisms feeding in gum tissue, and he references the late Hulda Clark, her Mexico clinic and books like Cure for All Diseases, including her hard line that dead or damaged teeth should simply go. His most personal story is a terminally ill man who asked to have old root canal and mercury work removed so he could die clean, came in with his two daughters, and was remembered in a phone call after he passed. He closes on vets pulling dogs' teeth for one to two thousand pounds."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Marc Mortiboys, better known as the Dental Shaman, joins InnerVerse to speak the truth about the tooth! What's so shamanic about dentistry and how did initiation elevate Marc above the dime-a-dozen dentists of the world? Tune in to find out, along with what teeth mean in the biofield, how PH comes into play, the Vegas nerve & gut health effects on oral regulation, and strategies for keeping your smile strong, and turning teeth around before the point of no return.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we talk about light and sound therapies, terrain theory concepts applied to the mouth, the link between gum disease and modern health issues, navigating the healing crisis of the mouth, the relationship between individual teeth and meridians, wisdom teeth wisdom, myofunctional therapies, and much more!

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "When the Healer's Energy Does the Work", "body": "Mortiboys opens the members' hour with the old idea of healing sages who never spoke, simply walked through villages and left people claiming cures, and he argues that a practitioner whose energy is right may not need to do much at all, the way a relaxed owner meets a relaxed dog. He thinks doctors and dentists overcomplicate things because ego and left brain love a heroic procedure. From there he asks what jaw tension is really about, claiming 80 percent of people grind or clench, that grinding leaves hairline cracks where bacteria lurk, and that more children grind now because of mouth breathing."}, {"title": "Frequency Medicine Meets the Hopium Test", "body": "Turning to what he calls shamanic dental care, Mortiboys praises the Activations by JJ channel and its light language track for teeth and jaws, recalls a mystic in Glastonbury telling him decades ago that he carries a Pleiadian walk-in soul, and places his thirty years of gongs and bowls beside ultrasound, MRI, med beds and EE systems. He admits he has never witnessed the online claims of prayer turning fillings to gold, and mentions Japanese drug trials aimed at regrowing teeth. Chance answers that anything is possible but he distrusts hopium, the promise that someone else will fix you, and prefers self-reliance."}, {"title": "Sunlight, Bare Feet and the Primal Lifestyle", "body": "Chance raises the point that followers of Weston Price fixate on food and leave out how the tribes he studied lived in the full range of natural light from morning to dusk. Mortiboys says British GPs are now waking up to vitamin D after years of stacking what he calls a Frankenstein cocktail of drugs, though he wishes they would test levels rather than guess. He widens it to fire bathing, forest bathing, going barefoot and the way rubber soles block the earth's current, then to Price's account of women softening urine cured seal leather by chewing it, which sends both men into a riff on urine as mouthwash."}, {"title": "Red Light, Terrain Theory and Leaky Gums", "body": "Asked about the sonic toothbrush on his website, Mortiboys says he is among the first to trial it, that its inventor is still a student, and that it pairs red light, long used on inflammation, with blue light that lightens the dentin beneath the enamel the way sun bleaches jeans. Chance offers a terrain theory reading in which so called pathogens are a cleanup crew that stands down once the environment changes, and Mortiboys agrees completely, recasting them as a SWAT team whose histamine overkill does the damage. He adds that we need some plaque, and that bleeding, leaky gums let oral bacteria travel through the body."}, {"title": "Meridians, Talking Teeth and Growing a Jaw", "body": "When Chance asks how a well meant sound therapy can seem to make a mouth worse, Mortiboys says his training taught that anything doing good can provoke a healing crisis, as homeopathy and naturopathy also hold. He maps teeth onto meridians, with wisdom teeth on the heart, canines on liver and anger, and incisors on bladder and kidney, conceding that peers who want double blind trials laugh at it. Chance calls teeth an early warning system for the organs, and Mortiboys urges patients to simply ask a tooth what it wants. He closes on chewing, nitric oxide, nose breathing and myofunctional therapy, with stem cell teeth as the utopian goal."}]
